title: CloudFoxable: access to a scoped secret
license_review: MIT; selected Terraform and root license were read. Provider/account terms and charges are separate.
check_meaning: The selected module grants ssm:GetParameter for its flag parameter to the starting user. Record that scoped access, an unrelated-resource denial and provider-confirmed deletion; a published flag string does not verify AWS behavior.
availability_reason: Creates real AWS SSM parameters and an IAM policy attachment. Account identity, provider lockfile, variable selection, cost budget and owned-resource teardown need validation. Fixed parameter names could collide outside a dedicated account; no account or charge authorization is configured.

runtime_acceptance: Dedicated account identity and explicit resource/cost scope
Reviewed selected module dependencies and naming
Failed deletion, retry and independently confirmed teardown

integration.check: Use a dedicated least-privilege exercise principal to compare the assigned and unrelated parameter; keep provider observations local.
integration.stop: Cloud billing can continue after the local CLI stops. Preserve Terraform state and inventory until deletion is confirmed.
integration.reset: Export work before discarding the owned environment and restoring its reviewed baseline. No reset is automated until lifecycle acceptance passes.
integration.export: Keep Terraform state/plan, credentials and parameter values locally. Import only this small observation report and hashes of the lockfile/inventory.
integration.destroy: Review the owned-resource destroy plan in the same dedicated account; run provider destruction and independently confirm the parameters, policy and attachment are absent before deleting state.

instructions: The selected module grants ssm:GetParameter for its flag parameter to the starting user. Record that scoped access, an unrelated-resource denial and provider-confirmed deletion; a published flag string does not verify AWS behavior. Use lab plan for requirements and the exact report template. Imports are manual practice observations and never enable runtime execution.
